reuse.why: Extends the existing getDateWithSkippedWeekend and RSchedule/recurConfigToRSchedule and adds a shared createHolidayChecker, but the daily-skip rule is re-written at each consumer instead of going through getNextDate or one shared helper.

duplication.why: The 'daily + skipWeekend -> drop weekend/holiday occurrences' rule and its '!isWeekend && !isHoliday' predicate are written three times (getNextDate, getUpcomingDates, getDatesInRange), and the weekend-move map is repeated again in getDatesInRange and schedule-template.

placement.why: Holiday checking and weekend moving sit correctly in shared/schedules.ts, but the daily-skip policy leaks into the server handlers and schedule-template (moveWeekends), outside the shared date layer.

scope.why: Changes stay on schedule date computation, the new handler, types and tests; parseRecurDate is touched only to carry frequency/holidays.

maintainability.why: Any further change to which days are 'off' or how daily schedules treat them must be repeated in several hand-rolled loops with ad-hoc lookahead limits (DAILY_LOOKAHEAD, count*7+14, margin = 2 + holidays.length).

bypasses_abstraction.where: app.ts getUpcomingDates and getDatesInRange filter weekend/holiday occurrences themselves instead of using getNextDate/getDateWithSkippedWeekend; schedule-template.ts computes its own moveWeekends flag.

disguised_duplication.where: The off-day predicate (isWeekend || isHoliday) exists as isOff inside getDateWithSkippedWeekend and is re-expressed as isWeekday in getNextDate and as inline filters in getUpcomingDates and getDatesInRange; the daily-skip branch is reshaped per site (find over take, filter+slice, loop with continue).

abstraction_drift.where: getDateWithSkippedWeekend gains a holidays parameter; getNextDate gains a frequency==='daily' special-case branch; getUpcomingDates, getDatesInRange and schedule-template's createScheduleList each decide the daily/weekend rule themselves.
